transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Zenova CTO), Marta Lopez (Zenova SRE), Irene Cho (Zenova Product)

Summary:
Quick sync to review pilot metrics from this week, confirm tuning changes, walk through cutover/canary playback, and align next steps for dry-run. Some latency regressions noted on p95 for longer sequences; team discusses routing and cache warm strategies.

Topics:
- Pilot telemetry and regressions
- Canary gating thresholds and SLOs
- A/B traffic split plan for model variants
- Runbook roles and post-cutover alerts
- Private deployment considerations and encryption/KMS callouts

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, let's do a quick roll call. we should have about 50 minutes, agenda in the invite. Samir you there?
[00:07] Samir Khan: yeah i'm here, hi all. Marta here too. thanks for setting this up.
[00:11] Marta Lopez: hey, sorry little late, laptop was updating.
[00:14] Priya Desai: no worries. quick note — i captured the revised telemetry dashboard from yesterday's run, i'll pull that up during the metrics section.
[00:20] Alex Morgan: perfect, ok first item — results review. Priya, can you summarize the p50/p95 numbers and any anomalies?
[00:28] Priya Desai: sure, so overall throughput looks good we sustained target rps, p50 is steady at 90ms for short prompts, p95 jumped to 1.1s on two peaks during longer sequence tests, those were the 2k token prompts. we saw increased kv-cache misses on variant-b which is the quantized 4-bit config, so i suspect cache eviction and the kernel path for quantized ops caused the spike. also a small rate of 429s during the 11:00-11:12 run due to a burst exceeding the configured continuous-batching window.
[00:58] Marta Lopez: 429s — is that from Redwood's rate-limiter or our nginx front? we saw retries on our side.
[01:04] Priya Desai: looks like it originated at the serving layer before the nginx. the runtime's admission policy tripped because the burst exceeded the batching target and the node dropped connections, those were transient. we can widen burst tolerance or provision a short burst capacity in Dedicated for the pilot.
[01:18] Samir Khan: ok that matters — we need predictable tail latencies. what's the tradeoff if we expand burst capacity? cost?
[01:25] Alex Morgan: yes cost increases a bit, but it's linear to reserved capacity we can propose a limited burst window of 2 minutes in the cutover where we allow higher concurrency. that'll keep p95 under target. i'll follow up with pricing numbers.
[01:36] Irene Cho: also curious about A/B — which variant was better for quality? variant-a is the fp16 baseline right?
[01:42] Priya Desai: correct. quality wise fp16 baseline had slightly higher nlg score on our eval set; variant-b reduced cost ~32% but had a few hallucination patterns on long context likely due to quantization noise. for rollout i recommend canary traffic for variant-b only on low-risk routes and use soft-fail fallback to variant-a if quality drift detected.
[02:03] Samir Khan: that aligns with our risk tolerance. what's the plan for detecting drift? thresholds? can we have auto-fallback?
[02:10] Priya Desai: yes, we have signal bundles — quality p95, token-level perplexity proxy, and a set of golden prompts. the plan: 1% traffic for 30 minutes, if quality delta > 3% on golden prompts or error rate > 0.5% then we auto-fallback to variant-a. we can wire that into the rollout policy in Redwood Console so it's automated.
[02:32] Marta Lopez: can we get an email or pager when auto-fallback triggers? we want human-in-the-loop before full rollback.
[02:38] Alex Morgan: yep, we can add a webhook to your on-call and a slack alert. we also recommend a quiet-window during the first 24 hours of cutover to limit large batch jobs.
[02:49] Priya Desai: moving on — canary gating thresholds. i propose these thresholds: latency p95 < 1s, error rate < 0.5%, golden prompt success >= 97%, and no more than 1% cache miss delta. default canary duration 30 minutes with a ramp to 5% traffic then 25% then full. thoughts?
[03:09] Samir Khan: the cache miss delta metric is new to us; can you explain exact signal? what defines 'cache miss' here?
[03:15] Priya Desai: it's KV-cache miss at request time for autoregressive decoding — when a request cannot use a warm prefix in the KV cache, we count a miss. higher misses spike compute and latency. we track it per model-variant and per endpoint.
[03:28] Marta Lopez: practical question: our infra has an internal burst gateway that routes requests. we prefer cutover at 03:00 UTC. does Redwood support region-specific quiet windows? our user base is mostly EMEA in that window.
[03:40] Alex Morgan: yes region-based routing is supported; we can anchor the cutover to a specific region and gradually shift other regions. the private deployment option can keep control plane within your VPC during cutover if you want tighter networking.
[03:52] Irene Cho: on security: are there any SOC2 implications with auto-fallback webhooks and logs? we need audit trails for the decision events.
[03:59] Priya Desai: yes all rollout events are logged in the audit trail with timestamp, actor, and reason. for Private we can stream audit logs to your SIEM and integrate with KMS for key management. we've done this with other customers.
[04:10] Samir Khan: good. ok runbook walkthrough — Alex, can you do a live playback of the cutover steps? start-to-finish.
[04:16] Alex Morgan: sure, i'll talk through and Priya will chime with telemetry checks. Step 0: pre-cutover checklist — backups, smoke tests, alert page — confirm SSO and user tokens. Step 1: open quiet-window. Step 2: deploy variant-b to canary pool with 1% traffic and enable golden prompt evaluation. Step 3: monitor 30m, if pass ramp to 5% then 25%. Step 4: if at any gate fail, trigger rollback to variant-a and notify stakeholders. Step 5: post-cutover validation and telemetry retention check.
[04:47] Priya Desai: for the telemetry checks, the exact dashboards are 'pilot/canary-telemetry' in Console. key widgets: latency histogram, golden-prompt pass rate, cache-miss trend, and model-error logs. i'll attach screenshots after the meeting.
[05:01] Marta Lopez: who is the on-call rotation if something triggers at 03:00? we need names and escalation.
[05:07] Samir Khan: currently it's me then Marta then ops. we'll send the final matrix.
[05:11] Alex Morgan: action: Marta sends the escalation list — Alex will ensure alerts go to that list. noted in action items.
[05:19] Irene Cho: about rollback — does Redwood support blue-green or traffic-split rollback? we prefer instant cut to baseline.
[05:25] Priya Desai: we support both. blue-green with DNS or traffic-split via the routing layer; can do instant reroute to pinned model version which is effectively instant roll back at the router level.
[05:36] Samir Khan: one more question on observability: retention of token-level logs — can we keep them for 90 days? we need to troubleshoot rare incidents.
[05:44] Alex Morgan: in Hosted default is 30 days, but for Dedicated/Private we can extend retention as an add-on. we'll include retention options in the pricing note.
[05:53] Priya Desai: let's talk about the dry-run on 7/29. we propose running the canary with synthetic traffic for 45 minutes starting 09:00 PDT, exercise long-context prompts and golden prompt set. we'll validate the auto-fallback and alerting chain.
[06:08] Marta Lopez: 09:00 PDT works for us, we'll reserve the ops team.
[06:12] Samir Khan: please include steps for key rotation and KMS latency checks in the dry-run.
[06:18] Alex Morgan: noted.
[06:20] Irene Cho: any outstanding security gating — SAML SSO is required by our compliance team, are we on track for SSO test?
[06:27] Priya Desai: yes the SAML integration is complete in the staging tenant; we have one outstanding metadata field around attribute mappings. Priya: can you send the mapping doc?
[06:36] Priya Desai: yes will send by EOD.
[06:39] (brief crosstalk)
[06:42] Alex Morgan: ok last section: A/B experiment config. we recommend running the A/B in parallel for two weeks on 10% vs 10% split after successful canary. track quality metrics daily and have a rollback plan.
[06:56] Samir Khan: fine. Irene, product will want the experiment matrix — i'll sync.
[07:00] Alex Morgan: recap time. Next steps: (1) Priya updates canary thresholds doc; (2) Alex sends pricing and burst capacity options; (3) Marta sends escalation list; (4) schedule dry-run 2026-07-29 09:00 PDT. that's all. any final questions?
[07:20] Marta Lopez: none from me, thanks.
[07:22] Samir Khan: nope, thanks everyone.
[07:24] Alex Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.

End of meeting
